questions.q: What does the seeded Corporate Card Transactions Report support?
options: Reconciling card feed transactions against what has actually been attached to expense reports
Setting mileage reimbursement rates
Creating new expense types
Approving cash advance requests
questions.explain: This report reconciles card feed data against attached expense report items, directly supporting the aging check on unassigned transactions from lesson 9.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of OTBI over the seeded reports?
options: It requires no underlying data at all
It replaces the need for audit rules entirely
It lets a power user build ad hoc analysis on live data by combining any dimensions, without waiting for a custom IT report
It can only show data that is at least one year old
questions.explain: OTBI allows flexible, ad hoc cross-tabulation of dimensions like expense type, employee, cost center, and policy flags, beyond what fixed seeded reports can answer.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a question OTBI can answer that a fixed seeded report likely cannot?
options: A highly specific cross-tabulation, like Client Entertainment spend by region for a quarter, limited to over-policy items split by waived vs. audited
The total number of employees in the company
The company's annual revenue
The current date
questions.explain: That kind of specific, multi-dimensional cross-tabulation is exactly the ad hoc analysis OTBI is built for, versus a fixed seeded report's limited structure.

questions.q: Why does good expense type and category setup (from Chapter 1) matter so much for reporting and analysis?
options: It doesn't matter; reporting works the same regardless of setup quality
Reporting tools automatically fix any classification errors
Expense type setup has no connection to OTBI at all
Sloppy classification (e.g. client meals miscoded as Miscellaneous) causes reports and OTBI analysis to quietly undercount real spend in the correct category
questions.explain: Reporting and analysis are built on the underlying classification; sloppy setup causes inaccurate aggregated numbers that reporting cannot self-correct.

questions.q: What question would the 'Expenses by Business Unit / Cost Center' seeded report most directly help answer?
options: Which specific pixel color an expense entry screen uses
How a department's travel spend compares against its budget
The exact GPS coordinates of a client dinner
An employee's home mailing address
questions.explain: This seeded report aggregates totals by business unit or cost center, which is exactly what a manager would use to track departmental spend against budget.
